name: Arizona

context: AZ 340: cover crop reduces wind and water erosion; best results when combined canopy and surface residue cover reaches 90 percent or more during erosive wind.
cover_rules: AZ 340: use current erosion prediction technology to set the cover needed, and time establishment to protect the soil in the critical erosion period.
AZ 340: sudangrass and forage sorghums need a lower rate when used for crop protection and wind erosion; some cover crops are not recommended below 3000 feet elevation.
residue: AZ 329: keep the crop interval STIR value no greater than 20, and do not burn residue.
AZ 329: to cut wind erosion keep a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
AZ 329: do not shred residue after harvest, since shredding makes it more susceptible to movement by wind.
barriers: AZ 589: trap strips are at least 15 feet wide when stubble is 1 foot or more tall in erosive periods, and at least 25 feet when under 1 foot.
AZ 603: herbaceous wind barrier rows are no more than 36 inches apart; barrier spacing is at most 10 times barrier height, with 1.5 feet minimum height.
AZ 588: cross wind ridges are placed within 45 degrees of perpendicular to erosive wind, spaced no more than four times ridge height; poor on sandy soils.
windbreak: AZ 380: a windbreak protects 10 times its height (H) leeward and 2H windward; choose species taller than the crop.
AZ 380: install temporary measures to supplement the windbreak until it is fully functional.
roughening: AZ 609: emergency tillage must give random roughness that cuts wind erosion by 25 percent, only on soils that form clods.
grazing: AZ 528: plan deferment or rest for critical periods of plant or animal needs.
AZ 528: provide adequate rest to enhance regrowth of desirable species.
drought: AZ 528: develop and document contingencies to prepare for episodic disturbances such as drought.
seeding: AZ 550: seeding rates are on a pure live seed (PLS) basis; rates assume 25 PLS per square foot, and 1.5 to 2 times that for broadcast.
